questions.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 7 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $-2$ times the second row to the first row.

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the second row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 7 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0+(-2)(5) & 4+(-2)(2) & 7+(-2)(1) \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(1)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1+(1)(5) & 3+(1)(2) & 0+(1)(1)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 6 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the first row to the second row.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1+(3)(9) & -3+(3)(6) & -2+(3)(-7) \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 28 & 15 & -23 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 28+(-1)(-2) & 15+(-1)(4) & -23+(-1)(-3) \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 30 & 11 & -20 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ 6 & 9 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ on $A?$
questions.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ means that we need to multiply the third row of the matrix by $\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{3}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ 6 & 9 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot 6 & \frac{1}{3}\cdot 9 & \frac{1}{3}\cdot -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the third row to the first row.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+5{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $5$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+(3)(2) & 2+(3)(0) & 1+(3)(-1) \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & -2 \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+5\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & -2 \\ -9+(5)(2) & 0+(5)(0) & -4+(5)(-1) \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $N,$ given by

$$
N=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1}$ on $N?$
questions.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $-2$ times the first row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}N & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2+(-2)(1) & 1+(-2)(-2) & 2+(-2)(1) & 3+(-2)(-1) \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 5 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 9 \\ 6 & 5 & -6 \\ -1 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ on $A?$
questions.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 9 \\ 6 & 5 & -6 \\ -1 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 5 & -6 \\ 4 & -1 & 9 \\ -1 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $V,$ given by

$$
V=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $V?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}$ means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4+(-1)(-1) & 4+(-1)(9) & 6+(-1)(-2) & 7+(-1)(6) \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 5 & -5 & 8 & 1 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another
questions.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $S$ into the matrix $T$, where

$$
S=[\begin{aligned}60 & 0 & 120 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}],\,T=[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 & 30 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd and $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $1$st row. 

By considering the given row operations that changes the $1$st  row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =[\begin{aligned}60 & 0 & 120 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}] & \,{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 & 30 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}] \\  & =T.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1}.
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $X$ into the matrix $W$, where

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -10 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $1$st row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $1$st row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+5\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -10 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =W.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+5{R}_{3}.
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $X$ into the matrix $W$, where

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $2$nd row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $2$nd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =W.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}.
$$

$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $U$ into the matrix $V$, where

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 6 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 6 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd row is the same in both matrices. The only rows that have changed are the $1$st row and the $3$rd row.   

By considering the given row operations that change both the $1$st and the $3$rd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}U & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 6 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & \,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 6 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =V.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}.
$$

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}2 & \,-4 & \,\,-2 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,4 \\ 2 & \,2 & \,1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & \,-4 & \,\,-2 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,4 \\ 3 & \,0 & \,0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}.
$$

$$

Therefore, the required row operation is 

$$

$$

$$

Which elementary row operation could transform the matrix $A$ into the matrix $B$, where 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071448/assets/56fd7e343edf6c26f36718a30f899af6c8eaf0cad5f6b07c90ffa93c19df6346.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has been changed is the $2$nd row. 

Now, applying the operation $R_2:=R_2+1 \cdot R_1,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4+1\cdot (-4) & 1+1\cdot (-2) & 2+1\cdot 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the transformation could be done by the operation 

$$
R_2:=R_2+1\cdot R_1
$$

or simply

$$
R_2:=R_2+R_1.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
canonical_examples.problem:
Given that
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071448/assets/59ee8e91d058e347238320a2bd5496630f33534564f67f901d2ddf89000f0108.png) which elementary row operation could make $a_{22}=0?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
In the given matrix, we have $a_{22}=5$ and we want to perform an elementary row operation that makes $a_{22}=0.$

- We *cannot* make $a_{22}=0$ by switching two rows, because there are no rows with $0$ as the second entry.

- We *cannot* multiply the second row by $0,$ because we are only allowed to multiply rows by *nonzero* constants.

- However, we *can* add a multiple of another row to the $2$nd row to make $a_{22}=0.$

Looking at the first row, we see that $a_{12}=1.$ If we add $-5$ times this entry to $a_{22},$ we will get $a_{22}=0$ as desired. So, the elementary row operation that we need to use is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1.
$$

Applying this operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1+(-5)\cdot 3 & 5+(-5)\cdot 1 & 6+(-5)\cdot (-2) \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -16 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the desired elemetary row operation is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1,
$$

or simply

$$
R_2 := R_2 -5 R_1.
$$
